title: Alphabet-matched padding separates representation effects from finite-context gains
submission_history: Measured locally on 2026-11-26; the pre-push heartbeat returned 410, so no PR was opened and the old lease was released. Resumed on 2026-11-28 under fresh lease 38c8d86aeeffa076059263d6. Original protocol, amendment, embedded code and measurements are preserved, including their historical lease identifiers. The normalization dependency vs/refcorpus.py is unchanged between the original measurement revision and the current base c9bb628. No re-estimation or selection based on later records was performed.
current_checkout_input_note: The current base tracks data as a symlink to an absolute private macOS scratch path; with core.symlinks=false on Windows this is a text file and data/raw cannot be created beneath it. The resumed verification therefore uses a separate padding-inputs directory containing only the four pinned reference files at their original relative paths. For this layout import matched_padding as m, set m.REPO to the absolute padding-inputs directory, then call its functions; the vs module and pin registry still come from the checkout. The retained original script is unchanged. No data symlink or production code is changed in this PR.

later_related_work.relation: Later source-aligned and inverse-model comparison; already distinguishes model state and smoothing from source-context reach.
Later matched state-specific interpolation and marker regimes on Latin works. Its results already support context effects in a fixed-state family.

Later Italian cross-work grid shows rankings change with order and marker regime. The present preserved German/French grid complements that result; it does not claim the denominator or finite-model caveat as novel.

statement: For reversible expansion controls, distinguish joint information preservation from the held-apart code length of a finite character model. On two fresh public reference-work pairs, in both directions, literal addB reduces order-8 bits per output symbol from 3.690–3.884 to 2.157–2.325; per original source symbol it instead costs 3.965–4.248 bits. The same observed alphabets and per-line expansion rates can also be achieved by deterministic or independent random padding. Low per-output-symbol rates therefore do not identify a cipher or an information reduction. Source normalization alone does not make finite-order estimates invariant: addB still improves source-normalized prediction by 0.122–0.296 bits at some lower orders in these four comparisons. All orders are reported; those minima are descriptive results, not selected models or new independent tests.
check: Reproduce the embedded public-reference-only protocol with the pinned corpus files. Verify every source-line inverse, exact output length per line and actual train/evaluation alphabet equality within each expansion group. Verify identity/substitution and addB/substituted-addB code-length invariance at orders 0–8. Compare both output- and source-normalized rates at every order and retain the disclosed initial support mismatch. Obtain the authors' transformation code before claiming full replication of the ambiguous alf/alfb suffix branches.

source.authors: Claire L. Bowern and Daniel E. Gaskell
source.title: Enciphered after all? Word-level text metrics are compatible with some types of encipherment

prior_work.relation: Already demonstrated denominator effects for one-step empirical entropy and verbose/padding codes; this does not claim that result as new.

Already reported held-apart orders 0–8 in Latin, Italian, Spanish and English with an inverse-aware reference. This uses new German/French work pairs, both directions, preserved physical line boundaries, observed-support matching, and a separately scoped vowel-suffix branch.

method_notes: Train on the shortest normalized physical-line prefix reaching 40,000 symbols in one pinned work and evaluate the prefix reaching 12,000 in a distinct work; reverse each pair as a second comparison. Context resets at each existing physical line. Empty lines remain. Gutenberg wrappers are stripped and each line is normalized independently. Historical edition front matter and notes are not manually removed; no claim is made that every selected line is medieval running text.

A fixed 0.5 base pseudocount and recursive backoff strength 2 score orders 0 through 8. These are held-apart predictive cross-entropies/code lengths, not unbiased Shannon-entropy estimates. No manuscript input or hidden membership is accessed.

Both alphabets and expansion match separately within the four letter-padding modes and the four suffix modes. Identity and fixed substitution are shorter baselines. The substituted addB alphabet is a bijective relabeling of the entire addB output alphabet, so all rates agree. The suffix substitution retains a literal c9 pad and need not leave rates identical, because source/pad letter collisions change.

The source-aware reference codes the original text and reconstructs fixed deterministic additions conditional on the shared published rule. Random letter pads add their measured independent-coin log probabilities; random vowel suffixes add log2(5) each. Fixed decoder, codebook and length/line metadata are shared side information and are not charged; this is a conditional representation reference, not a complete minimum-description-length comparison.

Uncertainty estimates and tests of statistical significance are not reported. The four directions share two work pairs and are not four independent language replications. These are deterministic descriptive comparisons at a frozen grid of orders.
scope_limits: Table 1 fully specifies addB. It specifies alfb's c9 vowel-final branch, but not which consonants receive B9 versus D9; alf also lacks its end-letter predicate. The suffix experiment therefore isolates only the explicit vowel-final c9 branch and leaves non-vowel words unchanged. Full alf/alfb are unresolved, not silently reconstructed.

The first protocol used ROT13 and random lowercase pads. Its declared support matched but its observed support did not: pads introduced q or w absent from some original prefixes. A recorded amendment restricts variable pads to existing vowels and fixes q/w in the substitution. Both measured runs and the amendment are retained. Revision followed examination of the first results, so the corrected run is not presented as a pristine preregistration.

Order-8 source rates are higher after padding in all four comparisons. Some lower orders improve after deterministic padding. A finite-order model can exploit a representation differently; preservation of whole-block information does not require its finite-order estimate to stay equal.
Nothing here decodes the manuscript, rules out language, reconstructs the authors' full transformation panel, or shows every verbose cipher is equivalent to constant padding.

protocol.new_contribution: Fresh German and French works, both directions, same declared output alphabet and exact per-line expansion within each padding group; source-aware rates and physical line boundaries.
protocol.input: Strip Gutenberg wrapper, normalize each physical line independently using pinned vs.refcorpus.normalize; retain line breaks including blank lines. Select the shortest prefix reaching the requested symbol count. Newline delimiters reset the character context and are not themselves charged.
protocol.model: Orders 0 through 8, recursive Dirichlet backoff strength 2, unconditional 0.5 pseudocount; fit on one work, evaluate the other; no model selection on evaluation.

addB_group.literal_addB: Append uppercase B after each source letter; leave spaces and line breaks in place.
addB_group.substitution_addB: Apply seed-408 bijective lowercase-letter substitution, then append B after each letter.
addB_group.deterministic_padding: Append B when the source letter index modulo 4 is zero, otherwise append the ROT13 of that letter.
addB_group.independent_padding: After each letter independently append B with probability 0.9, else a uniformly sampled lowercase letter. Seeds 40801 training and 40802 evaluation.
addB_group.inverse: Read each nonspace word as two-character units; retain the first character of every pair, and invert the substitution where applicable. Padding may share source letters because the framing is fixed.

suffix_group.scope: Only Table 1 alfb's explicit vowel-final c9 branch is replicated. Non-vowel words are unchanged. This is a restricted branch, not a reconstruction of full alf or alfb: the paper does not specify the split between B9 and D9, or alf's end-letter predicate.
suffix_group.vowel_suffix: Append c9 to a word ending in aeiou.
suffix_group.substitution_suffix: Apply the fixed substitution to source letters; append c9 when the original word ended in aeiou.
suffix_group.deterministic_suffix: Append ROT13(last source letter) followed by 9 to vowel-final words.
suffix_group.independent_suffix: Append a uniform lowercase letter followed by 9 to vowel-final words; independent fixed seeds as above.
suffix_group.inverse: If the word ends in reserved 9, remove exactly its last two characters, then invert any substitution. Source normalization excludes digits.

validation: exact round trips on all source lines and exhaustive lowercase words of lengths 1 through 3
identical per-line spaces and output lengths within matched groups
substitution invariance for every measured order
all orders and both denominators reported, without selecting the best order
declared and observed alphabets reported separately
protocol.source_aware_reference: Fit identity model on the source work. A deterministic invertible transformation costs the same source bits, conditional on the fixed public rule. Random padding costs identity bits plus the independent pad log probabilities. Decoder, protocol and codebook are shared fixed side information; these are conditional code lengths, not an unconditional cipher-length comparison.
protocol.interpretation: Distinguish whole-block information preservation from finite-context predictive code length. No manuscript data are loaded. Do not generalize any comparison to all encipherments.

amendment.reason: The first run matched declared support but not observed support: q is absent from the German forward prefixes and w from French, while random or ROT13 pads introduced them. Strict alphabet matching requires a correction. Retain and report the first run as preliminary, without claiming its observed alphabets were matched.

changes.fixed_substitution: Keep q and w fixed; seed-408 shuffle the other 24 lowercase letters. This preserves the missing letters discovered in the source-support audit.
changes.deterministic_padding: Append B when source letter index modulo 4 is zero, otherwise append aeiou[source letter index modulo 5].
changes.independent_padding: Append B with probability 0.9, otherwise a uniformly sampled member of aeiou. Same independent train and evaluation seeds.
changes.deterministic_suffix: Append aeiou[last source letter index modulo 5] then 9 to vowel-final words.
changes.independent_suffix: Append a uniformly sampled member of aeiou then 9 to vowel-final words.
changes.extra_validation: Assert equality of actual training alphabets and actual evaluation alphabets separately within each matched expansion group. Assert the same substitution invariance controls.

reproduction.script:
"""Execute the separately frozen protocol; public reference works only."""
from collections import Counter
import gc
import hashlib
import itertools
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path
from random import Random
import string
import sys

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO = HERE / "voynich-swarm"
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
from vs import refcorpus

PROTOCOL = HERE / "matched_padding_protocol.json"
protocol = json.loads(PROTOCOL.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
LETTERS = string.ascii_lowercase
VOWELS = set("aeiou")
ORDER = 8
substitution_letters = "".join(c for c in LETTERS if c not in "qw")
shuffled = list(substitution_letters)
Random(408).shuffle(shuffled)
FORWARD = str.maketrans(substitution_letters, "".join(shuffled))
BACKWARD = str.maketrans("".join(shuffled), substitution_letters)
MODES = ["identity", "fixed_substitution", "literal_addB", "substitution_addB",
         "deterministic_padding", "independent_padding", "vowel_suffix",
         "substitution_suffix", "deterministic_suffix", "independent_suffix"]
PAIR_MODES = set(MODES[2:6])
SUFFIX_MODES = set(MODES[6:])


def rotate(c):
    return LETTERS[(LETTERS.index(c) + 13) % 26]


def encode_line(line, mode, rng):
    if mode == "identity":
        return line
    if mode == "fixed_substitution":
        return line.translate(FORWARD)
    words = []
    for word in line.split(" "):
        if not word:
            words.append(word)
            continue
        if mode in PAIR_MODES:
            pieces = []
            for c in word:
                source = c.translate(FORWARD) if mode == "substitution_addB" else c
                pad = "B"
                if mode == "deterministic_padding":
                    pad = "B" if LETTERS.index(c) % 4 == 0 else "aeiou"[LETTERS.index(c) % 5]
                elif mode == "independent_padding":
                    pad = "B" if rng.random() < .9 else rng.choice("aeiou")
                pieces.append(source + pad)
            words.append("".join(pieces))
        else:
            source = word.translate(FORWARD) if mode == "substitution_suffix" else word
            if word[-1] in VOWELS:
                pad = "c"
                if mode == "deterministic_suffix":
                    pad = "aeiou"[LETTERS.index(word[-1]) % 5]
                elif mode == "independent_suffix":
                    pad = rng.choice("aeiou")
                source += pad + "9"
            words.append(source)
    return " ".join(words)


def decode_line(line, mode):
    words = []
    for word in line.split(" "):
        if mode in PAIR_MODES:
            assert len(word) % 2 == 0
            word = word[::2]
        elif mode in SUFFIX_MODES and word.endswith("9"):
            word = word[:-2]
        if mode in ("fixed_substitution", "substitution_addB", "substitution_suffix"):
            word = word.translate(BACKWARD)
        words.append(word)
    return " ".join(words)


def transform(lines, mode, seed):
    rng = Random(seed)
    return [encode_line(line, mode, rng) for line in lines]


def load_prefix(corpus_id, at_least):
    pin = next(p for p in refcorpus.pins() if p["id"] == corpus_id)
    raw_bytes = (REPO / pin["file"]).read_bytes()
    assert hashlib.sha256(raw_bytes).hexdigest() == pin["sha256"]
    raw = raw_bytes.decode(pin.get("encoding", "utf-8"), errors="replace")
    lines = []
    count = 0
    for raw_line in refcorpus.strip_gutenberg(raw).splitlines():
        line = refcorpus.normalize(raw_line, pin["lang"])
        assert set(line) <= set(LETTERS + " ")
        lines.append(line)
        count += len(line)
        if count >= at_least:
            break
    assert count >= at_least, (corpus_id, count)
    return lines, {
        "id": corpus_id, "title": pin["title"], "url": pin["url"],
        "raw_sha256": pin["sha256"],
        "normalized_prefix_sha256": hashlib.sha256("\n".join(lines).encode()).hexdigest(),
        "physical_lines": len(lines), "source_symbols_excluding_newlines": count,
        "words": sum(len(line.split()) for line in lines),
        "letters": sum(c != " " for line in lines for c in line),
        "vowel_final_words": sum(word[-1] in VOWELS for line in lines for word in line.split()),
    }


def score(train, test, alphabet):
    counts = [{} for _ in range(ORDER + 1)]
    counts[0][""] = Counter()
    for line in train:
        for i, c in enumerate(line):
            for k in range(min(i, ORDER) + 1):
                context = line[i-k:i]
                group = counts[k].get(context)
                if group is None:
                    group = counts[k][context] = Counter()
                group[c] += 1
    totals = [{context: sum(group.values()) for context, group in col.items()} for col in counts]
    bits = [0.] * (ORDER + 1)
    for line in test:
        for i, c in enumerate(line):
            p = (counts[0][""][c] + .5) / (totals[0][""] + .5 * len(alphabet))
            for k in range(ORDER + 1):
                if 0 < k <= i:
                    context = line[i-k:i]
                    group = counts[k].get(context)
                    if group is not None:
                        p = (group[c] + 2 * p) / (totals[k][context] + 2)
                bits[k] -= math.log2(p)
    return bits


def extra_bits(source, encoded, mode):
    if mode == "independent_padding":
        n_b = sum(word[1::2].count("B") for line in encoded for word in line.split())
        n_pads = sum(len(word) for line in source for word in line.split())
        return -n_b * math.log2(.9) - (n_pads - n_b) * math.log2(.1 / 5)
    if mode == "independent_suffix":
        return sum(word[-1] in VOWELS for line in source for word in line.split()) * math.log2(5)
    return 0.


def checks():
    words = ["".join(w) for n in (1, 2, 3) for w in itertools.product(LETTERS, repeat=n)]
    lines = ["", "a b c", "  a  e ", *words]
    for mode in MODES:
        encoded = transform(lines, mode, 40803)
        assert [decode_line(line, mode) for line in encoded] == lines, mode
        assert [line.count(" ") for line in encoded] == [line.count(" ") for line in lines]
    # A whole-word source collision is possible if digits are allowed. The input
    # assertion excludes them, so the reserved suffix marker makes inversion exact.
    return {"exhaustive_words": len(words), "modes": len(MODES), "round_trip": True,
            "spaces_including_repeated_spaces": True}


def run():
    results = {"protocol": protocol, "protocol_sha256": hashlib.sha256(PROTOCOL.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
               "amendment": json.loads((HERE / "matched_padding_amendment.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
               "script_sha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
               "controls": checks(), "comparisons": {}}
    for language, first, second in protocol["work_pairs"]:
        for direction, training_work, evaluation_work in (("forward", first, second), ("reverse", second, first)):
            name = language + "_" + direction
            train, train_meta = load_prefix(training_work, 40000)
            test, test_meta = load_prefix(evaluation_work, 12000)
            assert training_work != evaluation_work
            row = {"training_work": train_meta, "evaluation_work": test_meta,
                   "exact_round_trip_all_lines": True, "modes": {}}
            base_n = sum(map(len, test))
            output_lengths = {}
            observed_alphabets = {}
            for mode in MODES:
                encoded_train = transform(train, mode, 40801)
                encoded_test = transform(test, mode, 40802)
                assert [decode_line(line, mode) for line in encoded_train] == train
                assert [decode_line(line, mode) for line in encoded_test] == test
                assert [line.count(" ") for line in encoded_test] == [line.count(" ") for line in test]
                group = "pair" if mode in PAIR_MODES else "suffix" if mode in SUFFIX_MODES else "base"
                lengths = [len(line) for line in encoded_test]
                if group in output_lengths:
                    assert output_lengths[group] == lengths, (name, mode)
                output_lengths[group] = lengths
                alphabet = LETTERS + " " + ("B" if group == "pair" else "9" if group == "suffix" else "")
                assert all(set(line) <= set(alphabet) for line in encoded_train + encoded_test)
                observed = (set("".join(encoded_train)), set("".join(encoded_test)))
                if group in observed_alphabets:
                    assert observed_alphabets[group] == observed, (name, mode, "actual alphabet mismatch")
                observed_alphabets[group] = observed
                bits = score(encoded_train, encoded_test, alphabet)
                n_output = sum(lengths)
                row["modes"][mode] = {
                    "declared_alphabet": alphabet,
                    "observed_training_alphabet": "".join(sorted(set("".join(encoded_train)))),
                    "observed_evaluation_alphabet": "".join(sorted(set("".join(encoded_test)))),
                    "output_symbols": n_output, "expansion": n_output / base_n,
                    "orders": list(range(ORDER + 1)), "total_predictive_bits": bits,
                    "bits_per_output_symbol": [b / n_output for b in bits],
                    "bits_per_source_symbol": [b / base_n for b in bits],
                    "source_aware_extra_pad_bits": extra_bits(test, encoded_test, mode),
                }
                gc.collect()
            for pair in (("identity", "fixed_substitution"), ("literal_addB", "substitution_addB")):
                a, b = (row["modes"][mode]["total_predictive_bits"] for mode in pair)
                assert max(abs(x-y) for x, y in zip(a, b)) < 1e-7, (name, pair)
            source_bits = row["modes"]["identity"]["total_predictive_bits"]
            for data in row["modes"].values():
                data["source_aware_bits_per_source_symbol"] = [(b + data["source_aware_extra_pad_bits"]) / base_n for b in source_bits]
            row["substitution_invariance"] = True
            row["exact_per_line_expansion_matching"] = True
            row["exact_observed_alphabet_matching"] = True
            results["comparisons"][name] = row
            (HERE / "matched_padding_results.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
            print(json.dumps({"comparison": name, "source_symbols": base_n,
                              "order8_source_rates": {mode: round(data["bits_per_source_symbol"][8], 4) for mode, data in row["modes"].items()} }), flush=True)
    print("All frozen comparisons and controls completed.", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()
